articles.title: UAE firm to enter Indian energy market
articles.description: DUBAI — United Arab Emirates (UAE)-based technology company AIQ has signed an agreement to enter India’s oil and gas sector as it steps up efforts to expand beyond its home market, company executives said on Wednesday. AIQ will deploy its technology across the refineries, gas stations, and digital stores of an Indian oil and gas conglomerate, CEO Dennis Jol told a media briefing, declining to identify the customer. AIQ began exporting its technology 12 to 15 months ago and now operates in markets including North America, Kazakhstan, Egypt, Colombia, Malaysia, Vietnam, and Kuwait, Jol said. Formed in 2020, AIQ is a joint venture between Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. and Presight. It uses artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning to help improve profitability in the energy industry, including at Adnoc. However, AIQ still derives most of its revenue from Adnoc. All other customers account for about 5 percent of its business. “At the end of the day, you need an entry into this international market, which we are trying to focus on right now,” Chief Technology Officer Saravan Penubarthi said. The energy industry is increasingly adopting AI for cloud-based software, automation of remote operations and seismic data analysis to improve production and efficiency. AIQ also aims to pursue acquisition opportunities as part of its expansion strategy. “We sit on a ton of cash ... so deploying capital is definitely up front and center,” Jol said. AIQ’s partners include Microsoft, Nvidia, Amazon Web Services, and US oilfield services providers SLB and Baker Hughes.

articles.title: Left-backed protesters disrupting city's law and order: Delhi BJP
articles.description: Delhi BJP spokesperson Praveen Shankar Kapoor said on Sunday that it is extremely unfortunate that a handful of people associated with the Communist ideology are bent upon vitiating the national capital's political atmosphere and disrupting law and order.Kapoor, in a statement, said that the faces seen hovering around Jantar Mantar two or three times a day on Sunday are the same as the once seen during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) movement in July.He said that the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and its Communist allies are failing to even mobilise 50 people from Delhi."Even among those who turn up, videos seen on Saturday revealed that either one or two buses are being brought in daily from Punjab, or students from JNU associated with Communist ideology are participating and raising objectionable and uncivilised anti-government slogans."The Delhi BJP spokesperson said that posting a video of AAP leader Saurabh Bharadwaj being removed from the protest site on social media platform X is laughable."It is regrettable that AAP leaders, rejected by the people of Delhi, are today protesting in the name of the right to vote alongside the very Congress party that imposed Emergency and snatched fundamental rights of people.""Do the AAP and Communist leaders expect the police to allow them to act arbitrarily and disrupt law and order in Delhi," Kapoor asked.Earlier, Delhi BJP President Harsh Malhotra said that opposition parties such as the Congress, Communist parties and the Aam Aadmi Party, which have been rejected by the people of the country, are staging hollow protests against the Chief Election Commissioner."Through these, they (opposition parties) are vitiating the country's political atmosphere and putting undue pressure on the police and administration, while also damaging the business season that began across the country, including Delhi and Mumbai, from October 1," he added.The Delhi BJP President said that with the Assembly elections scheduled to be held in early 2027, the Aam Aadmi Party is already facing the prospect of losing power in Punjab, while the Congress is facing the prospect of a major defeat in Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Goa and Punjab."In such a situation, not only these two parties, but also the defeated and frustrated Communist, Samajwadi Party, Rashtriya Janata Dal and Trinamool Congress led by Mamata Banerjee have come together and are now attempting to derail the country's economy during the festive season," Malhotra added.The Delhi BJP President said that because of the protests by these opposition parties, the entire month of July was adversely affected from the perspective of business in Delhi."Now, with the renewed Opposition protests threatening to disrupt the upcoming three-month business season, Delhi's trader organisations are concerned. Several organisations have contacted us (BJP) and condemned these (Opposition parties') protests, which are being organised out of fear of political defeat."

articles.title: BSP seen hiking rates more than Fed, supporting the weak peso
articles.description: Japanese financial giant MUFG Bank Ltd. forecasts the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) to be more hawkish than the United States Federal Reserve (US Fed), with one hike this October, buoying the peso against the greenback despite its looming dismal performance through the end of 2026. MUFG Global Markets Research Asia said in its fourth-quarter foreign exchange (forex) outlook for Asia that the peso should take some gains from easing oil prices over time and a hawkish central bank. “This is nonetheless dependent on our assumptions on the trade deficit, Fed and US dollar, and domestic inflation trajectory,” the research arm said. Still, MUFG said it expects the peso to join the losing bloc in the fourth quarter alongside the Vietnamese dong. The Indonesian rupiah and Thai baht are projected to depreciate by two percent and 1.5 percent, respectively. It cited major threats that could further bruise the local currencies, including renewed oil supply disruptions due to the protracted tensions between the US and Iran. Other risks include “further increases in US yields, weaker global risk sentiment and a sharper slowdown in AI [artificial intelligence] investment.” Outperformers, meanwhile, include the Malaysian ringgit, Chinese yuan, and South Korean won, appreciating by 1.3 percent, 0.9 percent, and 0.7 percent, respectively. “[We] expect the Taiwan dollar and Singapore dollar to deliver smaller gains, while the Indian rupee remains broadly unchanged,” MUFG added. MUFG expects the peso to trade at ₱62.8 against the US dollar in the fourth quarter before strengthening to ₱62.5:$1 in the first quarter of 2027, ₱62.3:$1 in the second quarter, and further to ₱62:$1 in the third quarter. Last month, the peso suffered successive declines to record lows amid surging crude prices. The currency brushed the ₱63:$1 handle, hitting an all-time low of ₱62.86 per dollar on Sept. 14. According to MUFG analysts, the global lender’s less somber forex assumption reflects its view that the BSP will deliver “slightly more rate hikes than the Fed.” It particularly priced in rate hikes by a cumulative 50 basis points (bps) from the current rate of five percent. Last month, the Fed opted to raise its benchmark interest rate by a quarter of a point to a range of 3.75 to four percent. This tightening could force the local monetary authorities to extend their hiking cycle to widen or at least maintain the interest rate differential between the US and the Philippines, which now stands at a range of 100 to 125 bps. “We are assuming the Fed hikes rates once more, while for oil prices to gradually trend lower over time albeit in a more volatile fashion,” MUFG said, potentially bringing the Fed funds rate to a range of four to 4.25 percent. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, broke above $100 a barrel in August, weeks after the US-Iran war reignited following the expiration of a three-month truce. Brent traded above $102 per barrel last Friday, Oct. 2, as the likelihood of the US sending another aircraft carrier to the Persian Gulf intensifies the risk of continued regional tensions and disruptions to oil shipments. Domestically, MUFG bets that the BSP is “likely to retain a hawkish bias to prevent second-round inflation pressures, with additional hikes aimed at anchoring expectations and supporting peso through the rates channel.” While on a slowing trend, headline inflation has remained above the BSP’s three-percent target and four-percent target ceiling. Inflation clocked in at 6.1 percent in August, marking the slowest print in four months since the 7.2-percent peak in April. Disinflation may have ended in September as the BSP projects inflation to have rebounded to as high as 7.4 percent, potentially posting its highest rate in three and a half years since March 2023. For the BSP, price growth likely surged back to a range of 6.4 to 7.4 percent last month due largely to pressures stemming from food disruptions caused by weather events—including the successive typhoons that hit the country. Even as the peso stands face to face with elevated food and energy price spikes, MUFG said continued tightening, paired with offshore conditions, should anchor the local currency’s footing against the greenback. Apart from the lingering challenges, the Philippines could pin its hopes on some pockets of growth, including infrastructure and public investments. “Beyond cyclical headwinds, the Philippines still has supportive medium-term anchors from infrastructure, investment approvals and renewable energy projects, which should help underpin growth,” the Japanese lender said. Once inflation expectations are anchored and consumer price growth moderates steadily, the BSP could steer back to easing in the second half of 2027. That should rescue economic growth, which has been in a slump recently.

articles.title: DMart Is Sitting At The Base Of A Five-Year Structure
articles.description: Avenue Supermarts is again testing one of the most important supports on its long-term chart. The rising trendline started around Jan 2021 and despite multiple market cycles price has continued to respect this structure. The reaction from Mar 2025 was strong and when price returned again in Jan 2026 buyers stepped in immediately. Now in Sep-Oct 2026 DMart is testing the same rising support for the third time in less than two years. What makes this setup interesting is that while price has been correcting the underlying business numbers shown on the chart remain healthy with recent quarters delivering double-digit sales growth and improving EPS. Price is weak near 3800 but the long-term structure is still holding and this is exactly where patient accumulation can start before sentiment changes. If the 3600-3800 demand zone continues to hold DMart can gradually recover towards 4200-4500 and then 4700-4800. But the real long-term trigger remains the falling resistance near 5100-5200 which connects the Oct 2021 and Sep 2024 major highs. A breakout above that trendline would end almost five years of compression and open liquidity above the previous highs near 5600-6000. The important thing right now is not chasing momentum but watching whether buyers continue absorbing supply around this rising support. articles.title: Greenply Is Quietly Preparing For Its Next Expansion
articles.description: Greenply is sitting at a very important point in its long-term structure. After topping near 400 the stock spent almost two years under a falling trendline with every major recovery facing supply near this resistance. But the correction towards 180-190 in 2026 changed the character completely. Price reversed aggressively from the major rising support and recovered back above the 100 EMA around 275. Since then every dip near this moving average has attracted buyers and price is again pressing against the same multi-year falling resistance around 305-320. The latest consolidation is happening right below this trendline instead of price getting rejected deeply which shows sellers are slowly losing their grip. Even the numbers shown on the chart are improving with Jun-26 sales up 21% and EPS up 32%. Now 315-325 becomes the major confirmation zone. A strong weekly breakout and sustain above this area can finally break the lower-high structure that has controlled Greenply since its 2024 peak. There is liquidity sitting above the recent highs and a breakout can trap traders who are still expecting another rejection from this trendline. Once that supply gets absorbed the stock can quickly attempt 350-360 and then the previous major high around 400. More importantly the rising long-term support is still intact while price is holding above the 100 EMA. This combination of improving momentum, strong support and pressure against a multi-year resistance makes the structure very interesting. One clean breakout can shift Greenply from recovery mode into a fresh bullish expansion phase.

articles.title: This Four-Year Downtrend Is Running Out Of Space
articles.description: Laxmi Organic has been trapped inside a massive falling channel since the Apr 2022 rejection near 500. For almost four years every meaningful recovery has eventually failed below the same declining structure while price continued forming lower highs and lower lows. But the Mar 2026 low around 110-120 is showing a different character. Buyers stepped in aggressively from the lower boundary and since then price has started building higher lows instead of immediately collapsing again. RSI has recovered above 60 which shows momentum is improving underneath. Now price is sitting exactly where things become interesting — the falling multi-year resistance and 100 EMA are converging around the 185-200 zone. This is not just another small resistance. It is the area controlling the entire long-term downtrend. If Laxmi Organic gives a strong weekly breakout and starts sustaining above 200-210 the structure can change completely. It would mean price is breaking both the falling trendline and long-term moving average after years of weakness. That can trap traders who have become comfortable selling every recovery and bring fresh momentum money into the stock. Above this zone the next expansion can open towards 240-280 followed by the larger 320-360 supply area. The long-term liquidity remains much higher near the 480-500 zone which is around 170% above current levels. Reaching there will require a full trend reversal and time but that is exactly why this breakout matters. After almost four years of lower highs one clean structural break can mark the beginning of an entirely new bullish cycle.
